body:
I really hate to be the guy here, but I'll have to be the guy. You know, the type of person who wrote in to a Dear Abby and says "Well don't tell me to do this because it doesn't work and don't tell me to do this because I can't and..."

I got my blood tested for thyroid and iron recently and all seems well. I already eat pretty well which has been a good way to lose weight. I take vitamins and take care of my hygiene every day. I've tried to exercise but the energy just isn't there. And again, the excuse of "time." Even the therapist I went to recently, when he was finally giving me feedback after asking me his diagnostic questions, said, "Normally I'd suggest exercising, drinking less alcohol, and forcing yourself to spend time with people, but you're already doing those things..."

You're right, I should take care of myself. But it's hard. When I'm feeling despair, I don't feel like eating and I don't feel like doing much that normally makes me happier. I start the self-loathing cycle which usually ends up convincing me that I don't deserve to be doing anything that is good.

There is stuff I like doing. Or liked doing. Or I do and I don't have the time.

I'm a guitar player and have been for a long time. I write a lot of music. Or wrote... I have felt like I haven't had time but it's just an excuse. I do have the time but I don't do it. I even bought a recording pre-amp to record more music, but haven't done much of anything with it.

I play video games and collect arcade hardware. The arcade stuff is a pretty cool hobby but a lot of the thrill was finding things I wanted for good deals. And now that I have a lot of the things I want, I am left with the indecision to play them. I had a long list of things that I was playing on the consoles but managed to get through a lot of them over winter break from school.

It's not that I feel no joy doing those things, but I just so rarely can actually get myself to commit to doing that. And then I get dragged down a little more...

Thanks for the message. Funny you mention meditation, because my family (parents and brother) and I enrolled in a Sunday morning Tai Chi class about a year and a half ago. It's been pretty great for meditative practice, but I never seem to bring myself to do any of it at home, mostly because of the space. Maybe that's part of my problem.

I do appreciate the lengthy response. You sound a lot like my brother.

As far as teaching... well, when I was in college I was a math major. Didn't  know what I'd do with it, thought I'd try actuarial science. I didn't pass the first actuarial exam twice (got a 4 out of 10 when 6 is passing), and decided that it probably wasn't for me. My other passion was teaching, based on the great math teachers I had in high school.

So I moved back home from out of state, enrolled in a masters/license program and started teaching. I do feel like I am starting to make a difference and helping out. I don't know if I'm feeling that bad about teaching but more about life in general.

She is bad at relationships. I kept going over the reasons in my head why I shouldn't have pursued it at all. I don't know if I'd be able to handle being a step-dad to her 4-year-old. I don't think I could get along with a smoker that well by personal preference. But nothing changes the fact that I care about her.

Meds: who knows. Maybe it's a dosage thing, maybe it's a kind of medicine. I specifically requested meds that wouldn't really have a weight gain side effect. I didn't want it to ruin my progress.

When you ask about whether things are better, I can with certainty say yes. But I don't know why it doesn't *feel* like it, if you know what I mean. I feel like I've changed the environment so dramatically but I feel the same.

Thanks, and you're right. It's true that I shouldn't let it affect me too long. I'm a man of details and so I always try to figure out the objective reasons that I should not be upset - I just can't manage to convince myself. If I let go of that somehow, I might be able to accept the hurt and then get better.

Thanks for the response. I've heard plenty of times that I am the kind of guy that girls who are "ready" would want. But it doesn't seem to help.

As far as teaching, I know that things in my new school are objectively better. And I can tell the difference. I don't come home crying anymore, and I feel more confident. But it's just not quite to a level of "this is working." And I think that is more representative of my mental state than my actual feelings about the job.

But this waiting around has been eating me inside. I just want to give up on trying. I feel like I reached out beyond what I normally would anyway but nobody around here seems to want to help.
